transcript:
Header: 2026-04-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Oscar Rivera (Redwood); Jordan Kim, Priya Shah, Ethan Lee (NebulaCare)

Auto-summary: Quick, hands-on run through of Redwood Optimize qprofiles comparing INT8 and FP8 on NebulaCare's summarization prompts. Live console benchmark run showing p50/p95 latency and a small quality eval. Discussed rollout/fallback policies, KV cache impacts, and security needs (VPC / KMS). Agreed to sandbox run and share artifacts.

Topics: "Console Optimize walkthrough", "INT8 vs FP8 latency/fidelity", "rollout and fallback (FP16)", "sandbox and SOC2 docs"

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a thursday afternoon, um i'm Maya AE on the redwood side, and with me is Oscar our systems se, he'll drive the console demo.
[00:18] Jordan Kim: hey 👋 thanks, we appreciate it. tight agenda — we want to see int8 vs fp8 in action and understand risk for our prod summarization pipeline.
[00:25] Oscar Rivera: cool, so we'll go live in the Optimize console, run two qprofiles, compare throughput and then run a quick eval on 30 of your sample prompts, if that's still okay with the plan.
[00:36] Priya Shah: yep sent that smaller prompt set earlier this morning, should be in the link you shared.
[00:42] Maya Chen: perfect — quick housekeeping: we'll record the session, and action items at the end. feel free to interrupt.
[00:48] Ethan Lee: quick note from me — security first: we need to confirm KMS support and whether logs can be routed to our SIEM.
[00:56] Oscar Rivera: absolutely — we'll cover security briefly; the console also surfaces audit logs and you can tie into KMS.

[01:05] [Oscar shares screen] Oscar Rivera: okay, Optimize console — on the left you can see qprofiles. i'm loading the 'summarization-light' profile we prepped: baseline FP16, INT8 candidate, and FP8 candidate. just to call out terminology — FP8 sometimes shows up in the UI as F-P-8 in logs, and the kernel name in the stack trace is 'opt-kernel-fp8' which transcription sometimes munges.
[01:30] Jordan Kim: quick question — how does the KV cache behave with int8? we rely on prefix caching heavily.
[01:38] Oscar Rivera: good one — KV cache is orthogonal, but int8 paths have slightly different memory layout. For repeated prefix-heavy calls we actually see less delta because the cache saves token compute; latency savings show up mostly on the decoding path. so expect smaller differences for prefix-only workflows.

[01:58] Priya Shah: okay, can you show the batch-size settings and autoscale? our tail latency SLO is 300ms p95.
[02:05] Oscar Rivera: yep — profile is set to target 40 rps on a dedicated slot, autoscale min 1 / max 6, batch windows at 30ms. we'll keep concurrency low so you see latency numbers that match interactive use.

[02:26] [Live run: INT8 candidate]
[02:26] Oscar Rivera: kicking off INT8 run now. running 30 prompts, each prompt is about 40-80 tokens in the summaries.
[02:40] [00:00:30] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[02:45] Oscar Rivera: p50 is 75ms, p95 210ms, throughput 360 tps — these are server-side token times, note the console shows token latency and end-to-end.
[03:02] Jordan Kim: hm p95 210 is pretty good. what's the quality delta vs fp16?
[03:09] Oscar Rivera: we ran an automated BLEU / ROUGE-ish eval — for this dataset INT8 had a 1.8% drop on ROUGE-L compared to fp16, in human checks it was borderline acceptable for internal summaries.
[03:23] Priya Shah: 1.8% drop — curious how that maps to user-facing regressions. do you have examples live?
[03:30] Oscar Rivera: yes, pulling the console side-by-side output. (shares) you can see a few cases where dates or numbers get slightly truncated — that's typical for aggressive quantization on the value head.

[03:48] [Live run: FP8 candidate]
[03:49] Oscar Rivera: now FP8. this will use the same model variant with fp8 kernels.
[04:00] [00:00:35] Speaker 2: (typing)
[04:02] Oscar Rivera: p50 68ms, p95 165ms, throughput 410 tps. quality delta vs fp16 is ~0.6% on ROUGE-L, much closer.
[04:15] Jordan Kim: so FP8 gives both lower latency and better quality here? i thought int8 often had the latency edge.
[04:22] Oscar Rivera: it's workload-dependent. FP8 kernels on our runtime are more optimized for this layer layout — and for shorter outputs FP8 can win on both. int8 still shines in highly quantizable networks and when memory bandwidth is the bottleneck.

[04:45] Ethan Lee: can you explain the fallback story? say we ship INT8 and hit a fidelity regression in the field.
[04:52] Maya Chen: yes — you can configure rollout policies: start canary 5% on INT8, monitor eval triggers (difference in quality or user metric), auto-fallback to FP8 or FP16 if thresholds cross. Console shows a three-way fallback: INT8 -> FP8 -> FP16.
[05:08] Priya Shah: and do rollbacks happen automatically or require manual signoff?
[05:12] Maya Chen: defaults can be automatic but we recommend manual for enterprise. you can set auto-failover for safety-critical flows.

[05:25] [Oscar toggles into logs view] Oscar Rivera: note that kernel selection is per-shard; we also expose per-request routing headers so you can force a variant for debugging.
[05:40] Jordan Kim: earlier you mentioned batch windows — how sensitive are these profiles to different request size distributions? our traffic is bursty at 1pm daily.
[05:52] Oscar Rivera: profiles are adaptive — Optimize recommends batch parameters based on your trace, but bursts can push up p95; that's where autoscale and a small dedicated pool help. we also showed prefix caching which dramatically reduces work for repeated contexts.

[06:15] [Mini quality review — human spot check]
[06:15] Oscar Rivera: reading example 7 — INT8 lost a numeric token '2022' became '22', FP8 preserved '2022'.
[06:26] Jordan Kim: that's concerning for compliance logs. numbers must be exact.
[06:30] Maya Chen: agreed — for finance/clinical you'd likely pin to FP8 or FP16 for that route, or use a hybrid: quantize only attention weights but keep heads in higher precision — our Optimize console exposes those toggles.

[06:50] Priya Shah: hybrid profiles — can we have per-route qprofiles?
[06:54] Oscar Rivera: yes, per-route and even per-endpoint. you can map routes in the API gateway to qprofile ids.

[07:05] [Noise / cross talk]
[07:10] Speaker 3: (inaudible)

[07:20] Ethan Lee: on the security front — KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs — how are logs redacted? we can't have PHI stored in plaintext.
[07:31] Maya Chen: logs can be configured to redact prompt text; audit logs capture metadata and hashes. raw transcript logs are optional and can be sent to your SIEM with the encryption-in-transit and at-rest via your KMS.

[07:50] Jordan Kim: do you support HSM-backed keys?
[07:54] Oscar Rivera: yes, KMS integrations include HSM options; for private deployment we also support customer-managed HSM.

[08:05] [Bench continues — throughput stress test on FP8]
[08:06] Oscar Rivera: ramping to 500 tps for a short stress. p95 creeps to 210ms at sustained 500 tps; note this is a single shard in the sandbox; dedicated clusters will give better tail.
[08:25] Priya Shah: curious about cost delta — what's the typical cost per token reduction when moving FP16 -> FP8 -> INT8?
[08:33] Maya Chen: ballpark — FP8 can cut token-cost 25-35% vs FP16 depending on utilization and batching; INT8 can go 40-60% on certain models, but it's variable. Optimize gives per-token cost estimates in the console based on your qprofile and trace.

[08:55] Jordan Kim: can we see the console's cost breakdown per route?
[08:59] Oscar Rivera: sure — pull up the cost dashboard. (shares) here is token cost, kernel time, and batch efficiency. we also show projected monthly cost at current traffic.

[09:20] [Short pause]
[09:30] Jordan Kim: on evaluation — you mentioned an automatic eval. what metrics do you collect?
[09:34] Oscar Rivera: ROUGE-L, BLEU-ish, and a confidence score based on log-likelihood. for deploys we recommend tying quality alerts to a human-sample set plus a subset of production traffic using canary buckets.

[09:52] Priya Shah: do you support custom evals in the console? we have a custom QA scorer.
[09:56] Oscar Rivera: yes, you can upload scripts or link to an external evaluator; console will surface the results. we've had customers hook their own scorer (python script) and we run it against the responses.

[10:12] [Interactive: Jordan requests a forced run with numbers-heavy prompts]
[10:14] Jordan Kim: let’s try 5 prompts that are number-dense.
[10:19] Oscar Rivera: running INT8 first...
[10:24] [00:00:20] Speaker 1: (typing)
[10:30] Oscar Rivera: INT8 shows a few truncations again. FP8 preserves numbers. for NebulaCare's compliance routes i'd advise FP8.

[10:48] Ethan Lee: is there an auto-sensitivity sweep? can we automatically detect prompts that are high-risk for quant errors and route them to FP8?
[10:56] Oscar Rivera: yes, you can attach a per-request header or use content classification; Optimize can label requests based on regex or models and route them accordingly. that's the recommended approach for mixed-criticality workloads.

[11:12] Priya Shah: what's the overhead of content classification? that adds another step.
[11:17] Oscar Rivera: we do lightweight classification inline — it's microsecond-level if you use the inline rule engine; otherwise you can pre-classify at the gateway.

[11:30] Maya Chen: i want to call out an example rollout template — start with a 1% canary, monitor p95 and quality delta thresholds for 48 hours, then 10%, 25%, 100. include a manual gate after 10%. that's in the docs i'll share.

[11:50] Jordan Kim: what about model versions? we want to pin a qprofile to a specific model sha.
[11:56] Oscar Rivera: good, you can pin both model version and qprofile; the console shows compatibility matrix — if the model changes architecture too much optimize will warn.

[12:08] [Spot check — Oscar shows raw logs (slightly garbled)] Oscar Rivera: and this is the raw kernel trace — sometimes the console log prints 'redwood-opt-7B' as 'red wood opt seven B' in speech recognition exports, so ignore that artifact.

[12:28] Jordan Kim: any guidance on when to choose int8 over fp8?
[12:33] Oscar Rivera: choose INT8 when memory pressure is the bottleneck and you can accept small fidelity drops; choose FP8 when you need a better fidelity-latency balance. Also consider your eval thresholds and whether numbers/dates are critical.

[12:52] Priya Shah: for our timeline — we have a pilot in three weeks, production in 8 weeks. feasible?
[12:59] Maya Chen: yes — proposed plan: this week share benchmarks + console recording; next week setup sandbox; week after run extended 1-week pilot with 5% traffic; then expand. we'll attach docs for SOC2 and network config.

[13:20] Ethan Lee: cost model — during pilot, can we get usage credits or a trial on Dedicated?
[13:27] Maya Chen: we typically provide pilot credits and a temporary dedicated slot for evaluation — i'll follow up with specifics.

[13:40] Jordan Kim: any gotchas? we've heard about hallucination increases post-quant.
[13:46] Oscar Rivera: hallucination is more model and prompt dependent; quant can amplify rare token errors. that's why we tie eval triggers to both model score and human sampling. also consider keeping generation length caps and using conservative temperature.

[14:05] Priya Shah: show me again the per-token cost estimator.
[14:09] Oscar Rivera: (navigates) there — selects route, shows cost breakdown and projected monthly spend. note that batching efficiency line matters: if your traffic has low concurrency batching savings drop.

[14:30] [Wrap-up section]
[14:30] Maya Chen: quick recap: INT8 showed biggest cost savings but had some numeric fidelity issues; FP8 looked like best balance for NebulaCare's summarization, lower latency and minimal quality drop. action items and next steps as we listed — send spreadsheet, schedule sandbox, share SOC2.
[14:51] Jordan Kim: sounds good. please include the specific rollout template and remediation playbook.
[14:56] Maya Chen: will do.

[15:00] [End of recording — remaining minutes used for brief side discussion about support SLAs and contract term]

Side notes (garbled): "announced 95% SLO — uh, SLAs start at enterprise tier; bursts handled via burst pool oomph".

References shared during call: https://redwood.ai/optimize/benchmarks (link placeholder), shared spreadsheet: drive.google.com/nebulacare-qbench (placeholder).

End of transcript.
